clue.text: Chinese leaders after places in coup

indicators.note: after says the leaders come behind the places in the answer

parts.note: places, as a verb, means puts
the first two letters, the leaders, of the word Chinese

explanation.surface: Senior Chinese officials step into a seized regime after a takeover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'places' looks like a noun, sites of a coup, but it is the verb puts.
explanation.definitionFit: A putsch is a sudden violent attempt to seize government, a synonym for a coup.

clue.text: Bearer of message whose view is one-sided?

definitions.text: Bearer of message whose view is one-sided?

parts.words: Bearer of message whose view is one-sided?
parts.note: a mailed card with a picture on just one face and a note on the other

explanation.surface: A biased courier with a narrow outlook.
explanation.definitionFit: A postcard bears a written message and has a picture, a view, on only one side.

clue.text: In June days, son parched

indicators.note: In puts the son inside the number of days

parts.note: June has thirty days

explanation.surface: A boy is dry and dusty in the summer heat.
explanation.definitionFit: Parched means very dry, needing a drink, which is a synonym.

clue.text: Exercising self-restraint in Europe, for one

definitions.meaning: having control of oneself, especially sexually or of the bladder
one of the great land masses of the world

explanation.definitionFit: Continent is both an adjective meaning self-controlled and a noun meaning a large landmass like Europe.

clue.text: Myanmar city with Commonwealth subject going about

indicators.note: going about means surrounding, so the subject's letters wrap round the other piece

parts.note: a Malay, a person from Malaysia, a Commonwealth country
with can mean and, as in bread with butter

explanation.surface: A Burmese city visited by a citizen of a Commonwealth nation travelling round.
explanation.definitionFit: Mandalay is the second city of Myanmar, the former royal capital of Burma.

clue.text: Possibly Margaret Mead's defender touring wild north

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the defender wraps round the scrambled word

parts.note: an apologist defends a cause

indicators.note: wild means the letters of the word north are rearranged

explanation.surface: The defender of the famous researcher journeys through the untamed north.
explanation.walkthrough: Mead was an anthropologist, so the definition is an example; the 's stands for 'is'. 'wild' rearranges NORTH.
explanation.definitionFit: Margaret Mead was a famous American scholar of human cultures, an example of this profession.

clue.text: Part of crude model erected with cupola

indicators.note: erected means raised up, which in a down clue reads backwards
part of says the letters lie within the run of words

explanation.surface: Part of a rough model is put up with a dome on top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part of' finds DEMOD in cruDE MODel; 'erected' turns it upward.
explanation.definitionFit: A building with a cupola has a dome on top, so it is domed.

clue.text: Look at reduction limiting popular relief work

indicators.note: limiting means enclosing, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: lo is an old exclamation meaning look
in means popular, fashionable
a cut is a reduction

explanation.surface: Examining spending cuts that curb a popular aid programme.
explanation.walkthrough: Relief means raised printmaking here, not aid.
explanation.definitionFit: A linocut is a print made from a design carved in relief on linoleum.

clue.text: Annual youngsters originally read before Christmas?

indicators.note: originally picks out the opening letter of the word youngsters

parts.note: something read before Christmas is read early, ahead of the day

explanation.surface: A children's annual is opened ahead of the festive season.
explanation.walkthrough: Children's annuals are traditional Christmas gifts, but here one is read early.
explanation.definitionFit: Annual and yearly are synonyms, both meaning happening once a year.

clue.text: Peevish character's source of additional information

parts.note: peevish means irritable, cross
a reference vouches for someone's character

explanation.surface: A grumpy person supplies extra details.
explanation.definitionFit: A cross-reference directs the reader to another place for further information.

clue.text: Dispenser established around Greater London area

indicators.note: around says the word for established goes round the London district

parts.note: something established is set, fixed in place
Pinner is a suburb in the London borough of Harrow

explanation.surface: Some supplier has set up shop around a suburb of London.
explanation.walkthrough: PINNER is a district of north-west London, in the borough of Harrow.
explanation.definitionFit: A spinneret is the organ through which a spider or silkworm dispenses its silk thread.

clue.text: Delicious food from the big house, say

indicators.note: say signals that the words are spoken, so we want a word that sounds like them

parts.note: a manor is the big house of an estate

explanation.surface: Tasty fare comes up from the grand country house.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent MANOR and the answer sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Manna was the miraculous food from heaven in Exodus, hence any delicious or welcome nourishment.

clue.text: Conspirator's vessel impounded by Roman jurist

indicators.note: being impounded by something means being shut inside it

parts.note: Gaius, also spelt Caius, was a second-century Roman jurist, author of the Institutes
SS stands for steamship, a vessel

explanation.surface: A plotter's boat is seized by an ancient Roman lawyer.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of Conspirator's stands for 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Cassius was one of the leading conspirators who assassinated Julius Caesar.

clue.text: Extremist caught between both sides returning sharp answer

indicators.note: caught between says the reversed piece sits within the two sides

parts.note: the two sides are right and left, R and L

indicators.note: returning means the pieces for sharp and answer are read backwards

parts.note: sharp, of taste, means acid

explanation.surface: A hothead is trapped between two parties after giving a cutting reply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns ACID + A into ADICA, which goes between R and L.
explanation.definitionFit: A radical holds extreme political views, so the word serves as a noun synonym for an extremist.

clue.text: Sounds like Frost, but Poe's was sort of Runic

indicators.note: sounds like tells us to find a word pronounced the same as another

parts.note: rime is hoar frost

explanation.surface: A comparison of the poet Robert Frost with the verse of Edgar Allan Poe.
explanation.walkthrough: Poe's poem The Bells keeps time 'in a sort of Runic rhyme'; Frost suggests the poet but means hoar frost.
explanation.definitionFit: Poe's line in The Bells describes a Runic chime of verse, so the definition alludes to that quotation.

clue.text: Greed prompting rebuke at Westminster, for example

parts.note: a rap is a sharp rebuke, a rap on the knuckles
Westminster is a city, so it is an example of a city

explanation.surface: Avarice draws criticism in the halls of Parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: Westminster, home of Parliament, is officially the City of Westminster.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapacity is grasping, plundering greed, an exact synonym.

clue.text: Communication about damaged mail covered by insurance

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the communication wraps round the other piece

parts.note: a cable is a telegram, a communication

indicators.note: damaged means the letters of mail are reworked

explanation.surface: A message reports that mangled post is insured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' rearranges MAIL; the surface's insurance theme hides that Communication is a telegram.
explanation.definitionFit: Something claimable can be claimed for, as a loss covered by an insurance policy.

clue.text: Duty for Guards, somehow, not Greys?

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters are put together in some other way

explanation.surface: Only the Guards, not the Scots Greys regiment, do this duty.
explanation.walkthrough: The Scots Greys were a British cavalry regiment; sentry-go is the duty of a sentry.
explanation.definitionFit: Sentry-go is the duty of pacing as a sentry, which Guards regiments perform.

clue.text: Appreciative, given this much fuel?

parts.note: a fireplace grate filled to the brim with coal suggests the amount of fuel, and the same word means thankful

explanation.surface: Someone is thankful for a generous supply of coal.
explanation.definitionFit: Grateful means appreciative, and split it suggests a fire grate filled up with fuel.

clue.text: Theft from bishop putting out vestment on line

indicators.note: on means attached after, in a down clue placed below
putting out means placing around, so the vestment goes outside the bishop

parts.note: a robe is a vestment
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
RY, short for railway, is a line

explanation.surface: A bishop's robes are stolen on the railway.
explanation.definitionFit: Robbery is theft, especially by force, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Mosey along cutting ends off rose

indicators.note: cutting the ends off means losing the first and last letters

parts.note: a rambler is a climbing rose

explanation.surface: A gardener strolls about, deadheading roses.
explanation.walkthrough: Rose is the flower, a rambling rose, not the past tense of rise.
explanation.definitionFit: To amble is to walk at a slow leisurely pace, much as to mosey along.

clue.text: Nigerian bandleader with a following in Asian country

parts.note: the leader of the word band is its first letter, B

indicators.note: in says the pieces go inside the Asian country

parts.note: Iran is a country in Asia

explanation.surface: A Nigerian musician leads his band with a fan base in Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: Biafra was the breakaway state of eastern Nigeria, 1967-70.
explanation.definitionFit: A Biafran is someone from Biafra, a region of Nigeria, so the word names a kind of Nigerian.

clue.text: One may be nervous beginning to tackle weird sister

indicators.note: the beginning to a word is its first letter

parts.note: the weird sisters are the three witches in Macbeth

explanation.surface: A man anxious about taking on a strange woman.
explanation.walkthrough: The Weird Sisters are Macbeth's witches.
explanation.definitionFit: A twitch is an involuntary nervous jerk, so it may be nervous.

clue.text: Way composer gets round lexicographer

indicators.note: gets round says the composer's name surrounds the other piece

parts.note: Carl Maria von Weber was a German composer
ST, short for street, is a way

explanation.surface: A musician finds his way around a dictionary-maker.
explanation.definitionFit: Noah Webster compiled the American dictionary that still carries his name.

clue.text: Horse-drawn vehicle carrying knight in Roman garment

indicators.note: carrying means holding inside

parts.note: the toga was a Roman robe
N is the chess abbreviation for knight

explanation.surface: A carriage takes a knight dressed in ancient Roman clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A tonga is a light two-wheeled horse-drawn carriage in India.

clue.text: Man sounds almost obscene -—- he may be in for the high jump

definitions.text: he may be in for the high jump

indicators.note: sounds says the word is said aloud and a sound-alike is written

parts.note: Jim is a man's name

indicators.note: almost means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: nasty can mean obscene or indecent

explanation.surface: A man protests that he sounds nearly indecent before facing punishment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For the high jump' usually means about to be punished; here it is the athletic event.
explanation.definitionFit: A gymnast performs athletic events and might take part in a high jump, so the description is apt.

clue.text: Bond's modern connection

parts.note: a tie is a bond
in means fashionable, modern

explanation.surface: James Bond has a link with something up to date.
explanation.walkthrough: Bond suggests the spy, but it simply means a tie.
explanation.definitionFit: A tie-in is a link or connection, such as a book linked to a film.

clue.text: Tree concealing English kings in battle

indicators.note: in says the English kings go inside the battle

parts.note: Naseby was a decisive battle of the English Civil War, 1645
R, for rex, is a king, so RR is kings

explanation.surface: Monarchs hide in a tree during a battle.
explanation.walkthrough: NASEBY was the 1645 battle where Cromwell's New Model Army beat Charles I.
explanation.definitionFit: The naseberry, or sapodilla, is a tropical evergreen fruit tree.

clue.text: Punch required for one working in the sun?

definitions.meaning: a heavy swinging blow in boxing
one who makes hay while the sun shines, a farm worker cutting grass

explanation.definitionFit: A haymaker is both a wild knockout punch and a worker who turns and dries hay.

clue.text: Shed paraphernalia initially not required in battle (4-2) 23,169

indicators.note: not required in says a letter is dropped from the battle name

parts.note: Lepanto was the naval battle of 1571 between the Holy League and the Ottomans

indicators.note: initially says take only the first letter of paraphernalia

explanation.surface: Gear stored in a hut is not needed in combat.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove P, the first letter of paraphernalia, from LEPANTO.
explanation.definitionFit: A lean-to is a small shed built against a wall, so the noun means a shed.
